sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell-based APP metabolism assays performed with FlagM2-tagged full-length MT5-MMP (active and inactive forms); APP processing activity was measurable, indicating the tagged protein is expressed and functional at the cell surface.
sites.rationale: MMP24 is a type-I transmembrane protein with signal peptide residues 1–52 and a single extracellular N-terminus beginning at residue 53. The paper reports N-terminal FlagM2 tagging of the full-length, membrane-anchored construct but names no specific residue; because exactly one extracellular terminus exists (the mature N-terminus after SP cleavage), the junction is unambiguously insert_after_residue=52. Python confirms residue 52 is A and residue 53 is A. The tag is placed after the signal peptide cleavage site so it is not cleaved off, and it is ≥550 residues from the TM boundary. Full-length active and inactive MT5-MMP (MMP24) constructs, plus domain-truncated variants, were all fused with a FlagM2 tag on their N-terminal part and used in cell-based assays measuring APP metabolism (DOI:10.1101/2020.09.01.258665). The constructs are full-length and membrane-anchored.

sources.claim: Differential impact of MT5-MMP domains on APP metabolism To determine the specific impact of MT5-MMP domains on APP metabolism, we designed plasmid constructs N-terminally tagged with FlagM2 (FlagM2 + ), coding for full length (FL) active (MT5 FL ) and Δ inactive (MT5 ) MT5-MMP, as well as truncated MT5-MMP variants lacking functional domains as follows: catalytic (MT5 CAT- ), hemopexin (MT5 HPX- ), extracellular (MT5 EXT- ), transmembrane and intracytoplasmic domains (MT5 TM/IC- ), and intracytoplasmic domain alone (MT5 IC- ) (Fig. 4A).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are from the same paper and describe the same N-terminal FlagM2 tagging strategy; L1 is used as the primary supporting clip. L2 is redundant confirmation of the same site. L3 describes a 'MT5/GFP' fusion 'as previously reported'; the slash notation in the MMP literature conventionally denotes a C-terminal GFP fusion, which would place the tag in the intracellular tail (residues 624–645) of MMP24 — not an extracellular surface site. Because the referenced prior publications are not in the ledger and no residue is named, this is recorded in other_positions as an intracellular tag. No ledger line names a specific internal extracellular loop residue for MMP24, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: MT5/GFP fusion expressed in cells 'as previously reported'; the slash notation indicates a C-terminal GFP fusion, which falls in the intracellular tail (residues 624–645) of MMP24 and is not an extracellular surface site.
